newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks open sharply lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks open sharply lower on consolidation.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened sharply lower on Thursday amid a market consolidation and the blue chip Hang Seng Index fell 154 points, or 1.07 percent, to 14,267 in early trade.
The Hang Seng later regained some ground after finding support near the 14,200 level, standing at 14,383, down 37 points, after the first 35 minutes on volume of HK$2.70 billion.
"Blue chips fell across the board in early trade led by HSBC, but short-covering helped lift the index from its low," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J & A Securities.
HSBC was down HK$1.00 at HK$232.00 after earlier hitting a low of HK$229.00.
Brokers said sentiment had turned slightly bearish in the short term after some brokerage houses said they may downgrade Hong Kong in anticipation of a correction.
"The index is likely to drift down in choppy trade after a brief rebound," Cheung said.
